children: Shares of Maase jumped 5.9% in the afternoon session after the company agreed to sell its Glyken Bird Nest Technology (Shenzhen) subsidiary for $21 million in cash.

According to a filing with the SEC, Maase entered into an agreement on November 23, 2026 to transfer all equity interests in the subsidiary, also referred to as Shenzhen Glyken, to an unaffiliated purchaser. The filing stated that Shenzhen Glyken specializes in extracting small molecular bird's nest peptides using a physical heating separation method and manufactures and sells those peptides. Under the agreement, the purchaser will pay 30% of the cash consideration before or upon closing and the remaining 70% within 365 days after closing, with the transaction expected to close by the end of November 2026 subject to customary closing conditions.

Selling a business unit can bring in cash that a company can use to strengthen its balance sheet or invest in its core operations. Share prices often rise when investors expect a divestiture to simplify a business and unlock value.
The shares were trading at $10.02, up 5.9% from the previous close.
